faq.q: What does an AI fashion model photo show?
faq.a: Your clothing or accessory on a generated person. You start with a flat product photo and get a worn image for the store.

faq.q: How do AI model photos for clothing get made?
faq.a: Upload a photo of the garment laid flat. Choose an adult look and a scene, then make the image. Check the color and shape against the photo you uploaded.

faq.q: Can I put my products on a generated person?
faq.a: Yes. Upload the product photo, pick a generated adult, and download the worn view. Do not present that person as a real customer or a celebrity.

faq.q: Which products can I put on an AI model?
faq.a: Tops, dresses, jackets, coats, bags, jewelry, and glasses work from a clear product photo. Use a photo with the whole item visible, not a wrinkled one.

faq.q: How should I compare this with a studio shoot?
faq.a: You skip hiring a model and booking the studio. You still compare color, seams, and how the fabric hangs with the garment you ship. The photo does not replace trying the size on a real person.

faq.q: Can I connect my store software (an API) or run a batch?
faq.a: Yes. An API is a connection from your store software. You can send several clothing photos that way. Or upload them as a batch and reuse one saved look. Each image uses 24 credits, shown before you start.

faq.q: Can I publish these photos on my store?
faq.a: Yes, on a product page or a social post. Keep a plain product photo for measurements. Downloads have no watermark. You can use them on your store, in social posts, and in ads.

faq.q: Can I choose the look and save it?
faq.a: Yes. Choose an adult look, a pose, and a scene. Save that look in your brand library, the folder of saved looks, for the next release. The person is generated.

faq.q: Does the image prove how clothing fits?
faq.a: No. It does not show your size or your body. It does not promise how the fabric will hang. Publish measurements and a size chart with the photo.

faq.q: Will garment details stay the same?
faq.a: They should match the photo you uploaded, but small prints and seams can change. Compare before you publish. The guide to [model photos without a photoshoot](page:blog-model-photos-without-a-photoshoot) covers that check.
